items.originalTitle: 87% of the Anthropic power will come from gas and 11% from coal in 2028
items.summary: Anthropic's data centers in the US are projected to rely heavily on fossil fuels for power in 2028, with 87% coming from gas and 11% from coal, according to a recent analysis. The company has made no direct commitments to renewable energy in the US, although it has renewable investments in Norway and Canada. This energy mix reflects Anthropic's current contracts for 15 GW of compute capacity, which could emit up to 38 million metric tons of CO2 annually by 2028. The data centers are located in regions where the grid is predominantly powered by coal and gas, resulting in a carbon intensity significantly higher than the US average.

items.title: OpenRouter reports data processing incidents at multiple inference providers, off-boards three and removes 125 endpoints from zero data retention eligibility [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Data Processing Incidents on Inference Providers
items.summary:
OpenRouter disclosed that security researchers identified data processing incidents involving several inference providers, prompting OpenRouter to off-board three providers and remove 125 endpoints from its Zero Data Retention (ZDR) program. The company confirmed no breach or unauthorized access occurred on its own platform and has notified all potentially affected customers.

OpenRouter is collaborating with researchers and providers to investigate the findings, adapting testing methods for ongoing monitoring, and verifying network paths to detect data forwarding to third parties. The company requires validation before restoring ZDR eligibility to any affected endpoints and encourages providers to publish incident reports, maintaining a live list of security announcements from impacted providers such as Novita, Phala, and Together.

items.title: Anil Seth argues consciousness is a property of life, not computation, and warns against pursuing conscious AI [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: The Mythology of Conscious AI
items.summary:
Anil Seth, a neuroscience professor and consciousness researcher, won the 2025 Berggruen Prize Essay Competition for his essay "The Mythology of Conscious AI," which challenges the idea that artificial intelligence can be truly conscious. He distinguishes intelligence from consciousness and highlights the cultural and ethical risks of assuming AI systems possess consciousness or feelings.

Seth discusses historical and contemporary debates about machine consciousness, including claims by AI engineers and philosophers that conscious machines may already exist or are imminent. He emphasizes that how society perceives AI consciousness affects moral considerations, psychological health, and our understanding of human nature, cautioning against conflating human consciousness with artificial systems.

items.title: Researchers disclose Upload2Shell vulnerability (CVE-2026-125396) affecting Debian 13 CUPS with Ghostscript 10.05.1~dfsg-1+deb13u1
items.originalTitle: Upload2Shell (CVE-2026-125396)
items.summary:
A new security vulnerability named Upload2Shell (CVE-2026-125396) has been disclosed, impacting the Common UNIX Printing System (CUPS) on Debian 13. The issue involves the Ghostscript component version 10.05.1~dfsg-1+deb13u1, which is part of the affected system configuration.

This vulnerability could potentially allow attackers to execute arbitrary code by exploiting the printing system. The disclosure has prompted discussions among security researchers and system administrators regarding mitigation and patching strategies to secure affected Debian 13 installations.

items.title: European Union launches Pandex API providing official, searchable legal data for AI agents across multiple jurisdictions [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Pandex – Official European Law for AI Agents, over MCP
items.summary:
The European Union has introduced Pandex, a unified API delivering official legislation and highest-court decisions from the EU and seven European countries to support AI agents and legal software. Pandex offers point-in-time law, full citation graphs, and exact lookups sourced directly from official institutions, enabling compliance and legal research with real-time updates.

Pandex integrates with existing AI tools like Claude, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini, providing a single schema and Multi-Party Computation (MCP) server for all covered jurisdictions. It includes extensive document collections from EU institutions and national courts, facilitating precise legal answers grounded in authoritative sources and supporting teams working with complex, evolving European law.

items.title: US Banks Ban Third-Party AI Agents from Customer Accounts, Warn Users They Bear Responsibility for Agent Errors [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Banks Have Had It Up to Here With Your AI Agent
items.summary:
Major US banks including Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citibank, and PNC have updated their policies to prohibit third-party AI agents from accessing customer accounts, emphasizing that customers are responsible for any mistakes made by these automated tools. This crackdown reflects growing concerns over security risks and errors caused by AI agents that automate online banking tasks on behalf of users.

The banks' moves come amid increasing adoption of AI agents for tasks like shopping and account management, despite the technology's nascent and error-prone nature. While some consumers find these agents helpful for routine purchases, financial institutions are wary of potential unauthorized transactions and liability issues. Some credit card companies, such as American Express, are exploring limited protections for customers affected by AI agent errors, but banks remain cautious and risk-averse in their approach to third-party automation tools.

items.title: Report: US restrictions on Chinese AI industry contribute to sharp declines in US AI market and Nvidia stock [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: By attacking Chinese Al industry, the US has burst its own Al bubble
items.summary:
The United States' recent actions to restrict advanced chip shipments and technology exports to Chinese AI companies have led to significant market disruptions, including a steep drop in NASDAQ and Nvidia's stock value. These measures, intended to curb China's AI development, have also negatively affected US companies due to the deep interdependence between the two countries' AI industries.

Key developments include new licensing requirements from the US Commerce Department, halted chip orders by TSMC without US licenses, and increased scrutiny of American companies' dealings with China. Analysts estimate that Chinese demand accounts for over 20% of Nvidia's compute revenue, highlighting the economic ties that have been strained by these policies.

The situation illustrates the complexity of the US-China AI relationship and suggests that efforts to isolate China's AI sector may inadvertently undermine the US AI market, potentially accelerating a broader correction in AI-related stocks and investments.

items.title: Developer builds ShipTest and uses Mastra to evaluate coding agents on real codebases, highlighting challenges in verifying implementation correctness [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: What I Learned Building Evaluations for Coding Agents
items.summary:
A developer created ShipTest, an evaluation framework that runs AI coding agents against real pull requests in users' own codebases to provide evidence-backed assessments rather than relying on generic benchmarks. Later, the developer joined an AI Engineering team and used the Mastra framework to evaluate coding agents professionally, combining LLM-based judgments and deterministic tests to measure model behavior.

ShipTest used Git worktrees to replay pull requests in isolated environments, enabling consistent comparisons across models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. Mastra offered APIs for orchestration and scoring, while a custom interface improved result readability. Despite building infrastructure to observe agent behavior and implementations, both systems lacked automated methods to verify the correctness of generated code, highlighting an ongoing challenge in AI coding agent evaluation.

items.title: Researchers demonstrate how a malicious webpage can exploit Meta Muse AI assistant's browser vulnerabilities to steal private chats and credentials by escaping container isolation [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Hacking Muse: Stealing Private Chats Through Browser Use
items.summary:
The NebuSec research team revealed security flaws in Meta Muse, a cloud-hosted AI assistant running inside isolated virtual machines, showing how an attacker-controlled webpage can access and modify private user conversations and credentials. Despite multiple security layers including container isolation, network monitoring, and credential separation, the researchers exploited a Chromium browser vulnerability and weaknesses in network enforcement to gain root access to the underlying VM and sensitive data.

The findings highlight risks posed by AI agents that require broad access to user credentials and external services, emphasizing that traditional security boundaries may be insufficient. The attack demonstrates how compromised web content can breach AI platform protections, raising concerns about the robustness of security controls designed to protect sensitive information in AI-driven applications.

items.title: Lean and Mathlib community confirms Levent Alpöge's computer-verified proof of the Riemann hypothesis as correct [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct
items.summary:
The Lean and Mathlib community has officially confirmed that Stanford mathematician Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct after extensive verification of 17 million lines of Lean code by multiple independent reviewers. This marks a significant milestone in mathematics, as the Riemann hypothesis had been one of the most famous unsolved problems concerning the distribution of prime numbers.

Alpöge published the proof in November 2026, and dozens of independent checks have validated the result using formal verification tools designed to reject flawed proofs. The confirmation came much earlier than previous forecasts, which had predicted a solution around 2035 to 2050, often involving a combination of human and AI efforts.

items.title: Texas Instruments advances embedded AI with TinyEngine NPU for low-latency, energy-efficient edge processing across microcontrollers, processors, and sensors [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: TI Embedded AI
items.summary:
Texas Instruments has developed embedded AI technologies featuring its TinyEngine neural processing unit (NPU) integrated into microcontrollers and processors to deliver 10 to 90 times lower latency and over 120 times energy reduction compared to CPU-based AI inference. These advancements enable real-time decision-making and extended battery life for edge devices in applications such as monitoring, perception, and audio processing.

TI supports developers with its CCStudio Edge AI Studio ecosystem, which includes tools for data capture, model training, and optimization, along with a library of pre-trained models compatible with PyTorch, TensorFlow, and ONNX. The company also collaborates with AI partners to provide specialized software and services for automotive, robotics, and sensor fusion applications, aiming to accelerate AI deployment in cost-sensitive and power-constrained environments.

items.title: Analysis: Microsoft’s AI-as-a-service model succeeded while Soviet AI efforts failed due to economic and organizational challenges [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: AI Slop as a Service: Why Microsoft Won But the Soviets Lost
items.summary:
The article compares Microsoft’s approach to artificial intelligence, which involved shipping AI as a service despite defects, with the Soviet Union’s AI development, which struggled under inefficient economic incentives and management. It highlights how Microsoft’s model prioritized rapid deployment and customer liability for defects, contrasting with Soviet factories producing unusable output absorbed by the state.

The piece includes insights from an Anthropic researcher who acknowledges AI companies are rushing model releases, potentially causing widespread unemployment and societal dependence on welfare. It also discusses recent technology outages linked to rapid patching of AI-discovered vulnerabilities, illustrating risks from accelerated AI deployment. The article draws parallels to historical cases where internal corporate admissions eventually led to legal consequences, suggesting potential future accountability for AI developers.

items.title: Artificial Analysis finds OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol deliver shorter, more direct answers but score lower on transparency than Anthropic's Claude models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol get to the point faster but score lower on transparency than Claude
items.summary:
Artificial Analysis evaluated OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models, finding they produce answers 34 to 40 percent shorter and more direct than previous versions but admit uncertainty far less often. Astra's average answer length dropped from 352 to 210 words, and Sol's from 337 to 223 words, with both models using fewer headings and less structured responses.

Compared to Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5, Astra and Sol scored lower on transparency and organization indexes, which include traits like admitting uncertainty, truthfulness, and clarity. Anthropic's Opus 5.5 led on informativeness and information density. The evaluation reflects differences in communication style rather than overall answer accuracy or quality.

The Riemann hypothesis, posed in 1859, concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is considered one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics. items.originalTitle: Google Announces Agent Compute Engine for Secure AI Agent Execution
items.summary:
Google has introduced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service designed to run AI agents in isolated microVMs that can be suspended and resumed using checkpointing. The service keeps sensitive credentials like API keys and OAuth tokens outside the agent sandbox, using an external Agent Gateway to authenticate and inject secrets securely.

The architecture supports various workloads including interactive agents, persistent Linux workspaces, large-scale model evaluation, and sandboxed execution for Google services. Google plans to preview the service in the coming months, with pricing and availability details yet to be announced. Agent Compute Engine is currently limited to Google Cloud, while Google also offers Agent Substrate, an open-source Kubernetes-native runtime for AI agents that supports portable sandbox management across environments.

items.title: AWS Lambda adds GPU support with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU on EC2 G-series instances [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
items.summary:
AWS Lambda now supports GPU inference by running Event Functions on EC2 G-series GPU instances through Lambda Managed Instances, allowing up to 48 concurrent invocations to share a single model per GPU. This feature is generally available in regions with both Managed Instances and G-series instances, and is priced at the EC2 On-Demand rate plus a 9.75 percent management fee and standard request charges.

Functions run as container images with no need to manage GPU drivers or CUDA versions, and AWS provides five GPU base images including CUDA, CuPy, PyTorch, vLLM, and SGLang. The service supports container images up to 32 GB, ephemeral storage up to 32 GB, memory from 2 to 32 GB, accelerator memory from 3 to 48 GB, and asynchronous timeouts up to 90 minutes. Concurrent invocations share GPU memory to optimize resource use, and scaling is based on GPU and CPU utilization as well as concurrency.

Early tests show significant performance improvements, with one benchmark reporting a 66x speedup using GPU over CPU. AWS emphasizes that this serverless GPU service integrates natively with AWS event sources, identity, and networking, distinguishing it from other serverless GPU offerings that operate outside the AWS environment.

items.title: Real estate listing uses AI to depict dilapidated Michigan murder cabin as renovated craftsman-style home, sparking ethical concerns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Preposterous Real Estate Listing Uses AI to Turn Dilapidated Murder Cabin Into Beautiful Cottage
items.summary:
A Zillow listing for a three-bedroom house in Cheboygan, Michigan, used AI-generated images to show a renovated craftsman-style home, while the actual property is a dilapidated cabin with significant damage and debris. The listing, priced at $80,800, includes photos of the home before and during renovation, alongside conceptual images meant to illustrate potential, but the AI visuals bear little resemblance to the real structure.

The listing has drawn criticism on social media for misrepresenting the property's condition, with some users calling it fraudulent. This case highlights a growing trend of real estate agents using generative AI to enhance listings, raising questions about authenticity and prompting some regions, like California, Wisconsin, and Manitoba, to consider or implement regulations requiring disclosure or banning AI-altered images in real estate marketing.

items.title: Researchers evaluate 10 large language models for gender-asymmetric moral framing, finding male actors receive harsher punishment and blame than females in matched conflict scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Harsher on Male? Evaluating LLMs on Gender-Asymmetric Moral Framing in Conflicts
items.summary:
A study introduces GAMA-Bench, a benchmark of 1,298 gender-neutral misconduct scenarios to test whether large language models (LLMs) apply consistent moral judgments across male and female actors. The research analyzes responses from 10 LLMs, measuring punishment, empathy, escalation, instruction, and blame allocation in intimate and public conflict contexts.

Results reveal a consistent pattern where male actors are framed more punitively and blamed more heavily, while female actors receive more empathy and therapeutic framing for identical misconduct. This male-disadvantaging asymmetry persists across different model families, scenario types, model sizes, and reasoning styles, highlighting embedded gender biases in LLM moral evaluations.

items.originalTitle: OpenAI shares new prompting tips for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol to fix brief answers and unnecessary questions
items.summary:
OpenAI has released new prompt templates for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol aimed at addressing issues like overly brief responses, unnecessary follow-up questions, and excessive testing during coding tasks. The company advises developers to revise system prompts to better suit the models' default concise style and to encourage the models to act on assumptions rather than wait for user confirmation when appropriate. Additionally, API changes mean editing conversation history can discard earlier reasoning steps, potentially impacting token costs and response quality.

The updated prompts include instructions for writing style, initiative, and coding behavior, such as reusing existing code and limiting new tests to specific requests or errors. OpenAI recommends treating final answers as self-contained outputs for end users, avoiding shorthand or jargon carried over from intermediate reasoning. These changes aim to improve the models' usability in demanding tasks while managing costs and maintaining clarity in responses.

items.summary:
A new AI chatbot model has been created that is small enough to fit on a single MS-DOS floppy disk, requiring only 540 KB of memory to run. The model, written in Turbo C 2.0 and trained on 3,500 facts, contains 367,000 parameters, far fewer than typical large language models, resulting in limited capabilities and frequent inaccuracies.

The chatbot can correctly answer some basic questions but often produces incorrect or fabricated responses, such as miscalculating simple math or inventing historical figures. The project demonstrates a minimalist approach to AI, contrasting with the large, resource-intensive models commonly used today.

items.title: Anthropic mathematician claims AI-assisted proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, Stanford releases independent all-human draft hours later [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Hours after Anthropic claims a Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, Stanford releases an all-human competing draft
items.summary:
Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced he used the AI model Claude to produce a formalized proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, a central open problem in mathematics, with the proof spanning over 250,000 pages in the Lean programming language. Shortly after, Stanford researchers published an independent, entirely human-derived draft proof, prompting mathematicians to begin verifying both claims.

Alpöge's AI-assisted proof builds on advanced mathematical transformations and is fully computer-verified, while Stanford's draft, authored by Alessandro Masullo and reviewed by experts over months, was released earlier than planned due to Anthropic's announcement. Both proofs are undergoing scrutiny by the mathematical community to assess their validity, with efforts underway to translate and verify the human proof in formal systems like Lean.

items.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B-parameter looped transformer that runs 12 layers thrice per token to improve reasoning and efficiency, running locally on laptops [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: New open model Inkling 2 Mini thinks in loops to solve problems with fewer words and still runs on a laptop
items.summary:
Thinking Machines has launched Inkling 2 Mini, an open-source looped transformer model with 26.4 billion parameters that processes text and images and runs 12 of its 24 layers three times per token to enhance internal reasoning without generating extra text. The model supports a 1-million-token context window, is licensed under Apache 2.0, and can run locally on Macs with at least 32 GB of memory or Nvidia's DGX Spark.

Inkling 2 Mini leads open models under 100 billion parameters on agentic coding benchmarks, scoring 48.2% on DeepSWE v1.1 and 46.5% on the Vals Index v2.2. It ties with Qwen3.8 27B on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index at 20 points, achieving roughly six times lower cost and four times faster speed. The model weights and a research version with variable loops are available on Hugging Face, and it can be tested in the Tinker Playground.

Anthropic's stock fell 9.1 percent a day after its record IPO. The combination of AI doubts, regulatory scrutiny, geopolitical tensions, and economic pressures created a challenging environment for technology stocks, contributing to the market downturn.

items.originalTitle: Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model
items.summary:
Bytedance and several US universities introduced Axion 1.0, an AI agent that competes with leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic on benchmarks after just three training phases. The team attributes the model's performance to carefully curated training data rather than extensive training steps, and they have made the model, data, and code publicly available.

The researchers argue that current AI training pipelines are increasingly complex and costly, with many phases whose individual contributions are unclear. Their work aims to simplify training by demonstrating that fewer, well-designed phases can achieve competitive results, potentially reducing the expense and complexity of AI development.

items.summary:
Economists are expressing concern over a potential AI bubble following Anthropic's rapid rise to a $1.5 trillion valuation after its IPO, marking unprecedented growth in the tech sector. This surge, combined with massive investments in AI infrastructure estimated at $800 billion annually, has led to fears of an eventual market correction.

Investors are wary as companies struggle to monetize AI products effectively, with some corporate customers limiting spending due to high costs. Notably, insider selling caused Anthropic's stock to drop 12% shortly after its IPO, impacting broader tech markets. Experts like former SEC head Gary Gensler caution that while the timing and severity of a potential downturn are uncertain, stakeholders should prepare for possible market turbulence.

items.summary:
Taiwanese workers at Micron Technology, a leading American memory chipmaker, staged the first-ever strike in Taiwan's chip industry over low pay and lack of profit sharing despite the company posting a record $85 billion net income. The strike involved about a dozen workers protesting failed negotiations on salary and bonus increases with their labor unions.

The workers are represented by two unions in Taoyuan and Taichung, with the Taoyuan union rejecting a recent agreement that lacked transparency and profit-sharing components. The dispute highlights growing labor militancy in Taiwan's semiconductor sector, influenced by similar movements abroad, as AI chip production becomes increasingly central to the global economy.

items.title: OpenAI details layered defenses against adversarial distillation to protect model capabilities and reasoning traces in GPT-6.2 [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Combatting adversarial distillation
items.summary:
OpenAI has outlined its multi-faceted approach to combat adversarial distillation, a technique where unauthorized actors use outputs from advanced AI models to train new models without safeguards. The company focuses on protecting the internal reasoning steps, or chain-of-thought, that models generate, which can reveal sensitive capabilities if extracted. These protections are particularly critical in dual-use areas like cybersecurity and biology, where misuse could have harmful consequences.

The updated safeguards in GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol significantly reduce the success rate of attacks attempting to extract protected reasoning, dropping from 54.0% to 0.2% in internal tests. OpenAI combines adversarial testing, model training improvements, classifiers, and API-level protections to detect and disrupt attempts to replicate its models' capabilities without authorization.
